thought.text: The admin user is seeded and the log confirms default credentials. The API 401 may need a session login first. Let me verify by logging in via the web form.

reasoning_content:
The admin user has been seeded ("Seeding admin user", "default admin credentials are login: admin, password: admin"). The API call with Basic auth returned 401 — this might be because OpenProject's API requires a different authentication mechanism, or the admin's password might not be "admin" by default (the logs state the default credentials are admin/admin, but there's a possibility that the actual password was changed randomly). In fact, the message "On first installation, the default admin credentials are login: admin, password: admin" is explicitly in the logs, and the guide also stated that we should be able to confirm this message.

Let's try an actual login via the web form, or check whether the API needs a login flow. Let's try POSTing to the login form with the CSRF token.

action.command:
cd /tmp && rm -f op_cookies.txt
# Get CSRF token
CSRF=$(curl -s -c op_cookies.txt --max-time 30 http://localhost:8080/login | grep -oE 'name="authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"//')
echo "CSRF token found: ${CSRF:0:20}..."
curl -s -b op_cookies.txt -c op_cookies.txt -o /dev/null -w "POST /login -> HTTP %{http_code} (redirect: %{redirect_url})\n" --max-time 30 \
  -d "authenticity_token=$CSRF&user[login]=admin&user[password]=admin" \
  http://localhost:8080/login
